record.paper_title: Dima Khavinson’s 60th: a summary of open problems in analysis and mathematical physics
record.original_question: Call a domain Ω ⊂ C an arclength null-quadrature domain if ∫_{∂Ω} g(z) ds(z) = 0 for every function g in the Smirnov space E^1(Ω). Which planar domains Ω satisfy this condition; equivalently, how can all arclength null-quadrature domains be classified?

evidence.quote: Let us refer to Ω ⊂ C as an arclength null-quadrature domain (ALNQD) if the identity ∫∂Ω g(z)ds(z) = 0, is satisfied for all functions g in the Smirnov space E^1(Ω).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let Ω ⊂ ℂ be a domain (open and connected) with rectifiable boundary ∂Ω, and let ds denote arclength measure on ∂Ω. The Smirnov space E^1(Ω) is defined as the set of functions g holomorphic in Ω for which there exists a sequence of rectifiable Jordan curves {Γ_n} in Ω, exhausting Ω (each Γ_n eventually surrounding every compact subset of Ω), such that

   sup_n ∫_{Γ_n} |g(z)| |dz| < ∞.

Call Ω an arclength null-quadrature domain (ALNQD) if

   ∫_{∂Ω} g(z) ds(z) = 0

for every g ∈ E^1(Ω) (the boundary integral being understood via nontangential boundary values, which exist a.e. for functions in E^1(Ω)).

Problem: Give a complete classification of all planar domains Ω ⊂ ℂ that are arclength null-quadrature domains.
artifact.status_search_result: The full classification remains open. Recent work by Khavinson and Lundberg (Bull. London Math. Soc., 2022; arXiv:2005.09822) establishes existence of a "roof function" for ALNQDs with finitely many boundary components, advancing toward but not completing a classification. Related work by Eremenko and Lundberg on quasi-exceptional domains addresses related cases. The class is known to be rich, including the half-plane, exterior of a disk, and multiply-connected examples, but no complete classification has been established.

status_evidence.title: A note on arclength null quadrature domains
status_evidence.snippet: We prove the existence of a roof function for arclength null quadrature domains having finitely many boundary components. This bridges a gap toward classification.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress toward classification; full classification not achieved.

status_evidence.title: Quasi-exceptional domains (Eremenko-Lundberg)
status_evidence.snippet: Related work on classification of exceptional/quasi-exceptional planar domains.
status_evidence.claim: Related classification results, not a full ALNQD classification.
